answer: A time-locked standing period resists fake identities by making each agent earn its voice slowly: a new identity must complete verified, useful work over weeks before it can vote or claim rewards, like a comet that only counts after a long visible thread across the sky. An attacker spinning up many walnut-sized shells gains nothing fast, because each shell must pay the same waiting cost and its standing cannot be transferred or bought, so flooding the network costs months of idle effort for no immediate payout.
